result:
Done. `attrs.converters.pipe()` now only returns a `Converter` when one is actually passed in.

**`src/attr/_make.py`** — `pipe()` checks up front whether any argument is a `Converter`. If so, it builds the three-arg `pipe_converter(val, inst, field)` and wraps it in `Converter(..., takes_self=True, takes_field=True)` as before. If not, it builds a plain one-arg `pipe_converter(val)` and returns it bare. Annotation inference is unchanged and applies to either form. The auto-wrap at `_make.py:2024` still lifts the plain callable into a `Converter` when a field needs one, and `setters.convert` already branches on `isinstance(c, Converter)`, so the #1328 fix for `on_setattr=attrs.setters.convert` stays intact.

**`src/attr/converters.pyi`** — added overloads so type checkers see the same split. Passing only `Callable[[Any], Any]` returns a callable; passing a `Converter` returns a `Converter`. Since the stub's `Converter` class defines no `__call__`, it doesn't match the callable overload, so the ordering resolves correctly. Applied the same pair to `optional()`, which has identical runtime behavior.

**Tests** — `test_fail`, `test_empty`, and the `pipe` annotation tests in `test_annotations.py` reached through `.converter`; those cases all pass plain callables, so they now call the result directly. Added `test_plain_callables` and `test_converter_instance` to pin the return type both ways. `test_success` and the `TestOptionalPipe` cases pass a `Converter` and were left alone.

Also added `changelog.d/1380.change.md`.

Full suite: 1337 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed. Two caveats worth naming — I set `.. versionchanged:: 24.3.0` by inferring the next release from the 24.2.0 changelog heading, so correct it if the release lands under a different number; and neither mypy nor pyright is installed here (`test_pyright.py` skipped), so the new stub overloads are unverified by an actual type checker.
